title: Section 4: Leave and Absence

headings.text: 4.4 Types of leave at a glance

key_sentences: This section explains how much leave you are entitled to, how to request it and what happens when you are unable to work.
Your entitlement depends on your length of service on 1 January of the leave year.
Leave must be approved by your line manager before it is booked.
You can also use the command line tool:
The following rules apply to all requests:
Directors publish the peak calendar in November for the following year, and requests made before then are accepted on a first come, first served basis.
If you have taken more leave than you have earned, the difference is deducted from your final pay.
Staff who are required to work on a public holiday receive a day in lieu.
Sick pay is paid in full for the first 26 weeks in any rolling twelve months.
Questions about this section should be sent to the People team, who will reply within two working days.

rows: Yes, up to 10 days per year
Half pay for up to 3 months

list_items.text: (a) No more than ten consecutive working days may be taken without the written agreement of a director.
(b) Leave over the year end is handled as follows:
(i) days carried over must be taken by 31 March;
(ii) days not taken by that date lapse without payment.
(c) Teams must agree cover for client work before leave starts.
1) Telephone your line manager; a message left with a colleague is not enough.
2) Keep the manager informed every three days if the absence continues.
3) Send a medical note to HR from the eighth calendar day.
